name: duckduckgo/shopping
description: Search DuckDuckGo Shopping by keyword and get product listings with title, price, merchant, rating and link, by region.

q.description: Parameter defines the query you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular DuckDuckGo Shopping search. Parameter length can not exceed 500 characters.

kl.description: Parameter defines the region to use for the DuckDuckGo Shopping search. It sets the stores, the language, and the currency of the products. Region code examples: `us-en` (default) for the United States, `uk-en` for United Kingdom, or `fr-fr` for France. Head to the DuckDuckGo Shopping regions for a full list of supported regions.

filters.description: Parameter defines the filters to apply, like a brand, a price range, or a store. You can find its value in `filters` of the results: each option has a `value`. To combine filters, apply them one at a time, like on DuckDuckGo: in the results of a filtered search, the `value` of each option includes the filters already applied. For example, search with the `value` of the brand `Cuisinart`, then with the `value` of the price range `Up to $100` from these results, to get Cuisinart products up to $100. Don't join values yourself: DuckDuckGo may apply only some of them.

sort_by.description: Parameter defines the sorting order of the results. It defaults to DuckDuckGo's featured order. Available options: `1` - Price: low to high `2` - Price: high to low

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.

next_page_token.description: Parameter defines the next page token. It is used for retrieving the next page of results, like scrolling down on DuckDuckGo Shopping. Up to 30 results are returned per page. The next page token can be found in the the API JSON response: `the API_pagination -> next_page_token`

# DuckDuckGo Shopping

Search DuckDuckGo Shopping by keyword and get product listings with title, price, merchant, rating and link, by region.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/duckduckgo/shopping" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"q": "airpods"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data` as structured JSON.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `sort_by` | string | No | Parameter defines the sorting order of the results. It defaults to DuckDuckGo's featured order. Available options: `1` - Price: low to high `2` - Price: high to low |
| `filters` | string | No | Parameter defines the filters to apply, like a brand, a price range, or a store. You can find its value in `filters` of the results: each option has a `value`. To combine filters, apply them one at a time, like on DuckDuckGo: in the results |
| `next_page_token` | string | No | Parameter defines the next page token. It is used for retrieving the next page of results, like scrolling down on DuckDuckGo Shopping. Up to 30 results are returned per page. The next page token can be found in the the API JSON response: `t |
| `json_restrictor` | string | No | Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details. |

## Pricing

$0.010 per successful call. Failed calls are not charged.
